title: Playing after-hours parties for visiting big bands; Joe Thomas as mentor
summary: Larkin's band played the after parties for Lunceford, Ellington, Basie and others in Houston; Chu Berry wouldn't explain his tricks but Joe Thomas shared everything.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: But now, let me get back to you ... we played all the after parties. For every big band that came in to Houston, we had maybe two a month. The Luntzwood Luntz Ford band was one of them that come in -- the Duke Ellington Band, Count Basie, the Millinder Claude Hopkins, the Tiny Bradshaws, the Lucky Milliner -- we played all the after parties. Now what we did -- the after parties didn't start until after midnight, but we had access of going up to hear to go up and hearing all the bands opened till midnight -- twelve o'clock ... and they closed at one. Now we got to go and get
set to meet them and the people coming from the dance.

Now this is how the Joe Thomas's come along, the Cab Callows, the Count Basies -- all of them made the after parties. And Joe and I got to be real tight. Chu Berry was with Cab Calloway then, and they all would come up and they'd jam with us and what have you -- and he sat beside me and he went up and made one of those off the horn notes, and I would say, "How do you make that?" -- and he would say, "I just do it." Didn't encourage me ... I'm a youngster. But he didn't tell you nothing.

But Joe Thomas would tell you everything he knew. So I had a double situation there with Joe -- loved his playing, his showmanship, plus he would talk to you and tell you things. So to me, he was like a father. And we ended up being very good friends, and when I got to New York -- well, I was with Lionel Hampton and he was with Luntz Ford, and they got married here in Philadelphia, and I was supposed to be his best man, because I was working at Fay's Theatre and had a break and couldn't get there and I sent my wife just to pinch hit for me 'cause I couldn't make it.
